question: Does a strong-chorus record at the same physical SiteID remain predictive of later wet-survey strong chorus after a multi-year gap, or is local chorus memory only short-lived?
population: Physically stable matched pairs with at least one prior eligible run in the same State x RouteNumber x RunNumber stratum. Focal species are route-new in the wet survey and had occurred somewhere on the route in prior years.
unit: pair x focal species x physical stop

memory_age.recent: Most recent prior CallingIndex 2-3 record for the species at this SiteID occurred 1-3 years before the earlier focal-pair year.
memory_age.old: Most recent prior CallingIndex 2-3 record occurred >=4 years before the earlier focal-pair year.
memory_age.none: No prior CallingIndex 2-3 record for the species at this SiteID.

primary_design: Within each pair x species, regress wet_strong (CI2-3) on recent-memory and old-memory indicators after exact within-group demeaning; no intercept; cluster covariance by State x RouteNumber.
secondary: Recent-memory coefficient and wet_full (CI3) coefficients are reported descriptively.
Among stops with prior strong memory, report continuous years-since-last-strong slope as a descriptive decay estimate; no pass gate.
minimum_gate: At least 300 informative pair x species groups containing both old-memory and none stops, >=200 routes, >=20 species.
interpretation: Positive old-memory targeting supports a durable local acoustic template compatible with persistent habitat suitability or local population recurrence.
It does not prove continuous occupancy, site fidelity of individuals, biological memory, or the same individuals returning.
No causal rainfall or breeding-success claim.
